questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had friends who had been in Bologna on exchange and really liked it. Furthermore, I have always been curious on Italian culture and the University had some really interesting courses within climate and sustainability.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Information was provided sufficiently but at times you felt a little behind because some information was provided very late compared to other universities.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: University of Bologna have a great help desk which is very helpful. You can log in easy and get help over zoom calls. Very smart and I strongly recommend to use this service.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I had connections through friends and because of this I was able to have housing easily but it can be difficult if you do not have direct contacts. I recommend reaching out to agencies because they have a lot of different housing. It is important to consider that you get what you pay for so cheaper housing may also mean you will live in poor condition housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Try to get housing within the "city walls" as everything happens here for most people and you can access all relevant parts of the city from here. All parts of the city have their own energy. The north part of the city is a little bit more rough but also have a cool energy. The southern part is more clean and look more expensive even though you can get okay cheap accomendation if you are lucky. I would recommend areas around Via del Pratello or Piazza Aldrovandi.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get relevant links and your mail address are easily accesible. Very easy but a lot of the information was given late. Signing up for courses can be done in the beginning of the semester and you will be able change courses which is a nice option different from my home university. But then when you need to register for the courses you have actually chosen it is very manual in the system.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help desk was available very fast and easy help. You can also write mails but answer time is often very slow.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Went fine but I felt a little insecure during the process because you do not get that many confirmations which states if you have done it correctly.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the help desk if you have any questions and better earlier than to late.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The course level was easily observable. It was mandatory for me to take second cycle / master courses because I am a master student.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Very different. Exams were often multiple choice and essay questions. More discussion based but not always that it worked effectively because students were not engaged in these discussions. 
In general the level was less challenging.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Development and Climate Change
Fundamentals of Artificial Intelligence
Political Ecology of Work
Education Systems and Policies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Fundamentals of Artificial Intelligence is a good course if you are curious on this technology but does not have that much knowledge on the subject beforehand. But it requires some work and only take this course if you have intuitive understanding of logic and math.

Development and Climate change is a good course to understand the consequences of climate change and how these effect different groups around the world.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected. Fairly cheap but you end using more money than expected if you like going to restaurants.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Fitness and culture.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that much directly offered by the university but ESN bologna offers a lot of events, sports and trips.  But I did not prefer this option as I am in mid twenties and most people attending these events and trips were in the early twenties.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the cinema modernissimo. Very much also a city for food lovers. Go searching for second hand stores. And the Bologna matches on the stadium is a must try experience.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go visit the cities around Bologna especially some of the smaller. I went to Lambrusco festival in Castelvetro di Modena which was very cool. Flixbus is very cheap.
You can get to so many amazing places. The mountains in the Dolomites and city of Ancona was some of my favourite places.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
If you can learn some Italian! Hard to socialize with locals in english even though most speak some english.
Life is slower in Italy but embrace it and get inspired.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Try finding some events without alcohol. Parties is always fun and a good way to find new friends, but if your only community is through alcohol this will get unhealthy.
ESN is a good place start and socialize with your roommates.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Italians will often say that we will find out a long the way which can be stressing for Danes because we always plan long a head. I see myself as a person who do not plan that much but even I got frustrated sometimes.

But try to accept this and see it as part of your Italian experience and maybe also try to get inspired.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really like the honesty you feel when talking to Italians who are more straightforward than many cultures. Furthermore, the food and wine are amazing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do not stress over the differences between the university systems. Everythin will most likely work out along the way and many things are determined doing the beginning of the semester. Things which would be determined and registred before the semester in Copenhagen.

Find accomendation early. It is good way to feel secure and be certain that you have your "base". 

Remember to enjoy the city in your own way. If you do not know any who want to do the same things as you then do it alone. The time go faster than you expect.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The city is very walkable so you can always explore or walk by foot but the city bikes RideMovi also works very good.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Travelling, food and simply experiencing living in Bologna.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The bureaucracy stressed me out but there is only way forward and that is to talk to other students and ask questions.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
